claims.claim_vi: Redis is a data structures server that stores data on disk, and can be thought of as a more complex memcached whose operations are not just SETs and GETs but work on lists, sets and ordered structures.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of redis/redis at tag 7.0.15 (commit f35f36a265403c07b119830aa4bb3b7d71653ec9), the version that was run.

claims.claim_vi: memcached is a high performance multithreaded event-based key/value cache store; it does non-blocking network I/O, but not disk.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of memcached/memcached at tag 1.6.24 (commit 1b3b8555734f9b7b8d979924c7f8d6cf82194ba8), the version that was run.

claims.claim_vi: memcached 1.6.24 defaults: set/get of a string works; incr on '1' gives 2; 'hset' returns ERROR; a 2 MiB value gives SERVER_ERROR object too large for cache while 900 KiB is stored; item_size_max 1048576; 4 threads; 64 MiB memory limit; after a restart the key is gone. With -m 2, 5,000 sets of 1000 bytes all stored with 3,230 evictions; with -M, 1,770 stored and 3,230 SERVER_ERROR out of memory storing object.
claims.verified_by: Experiment run by the author on 2026-10-18 on one KVM virtual machine (4 vCPU): memcached 1.6.24 (Ubuntu package) driven over its text protocol from Python; stats and stats settings read.

claims.claim_vi: Redis 7.0.15: a 2 MiB SET succeeds (proto-max-bulk-len 536870912); after SAVE and a restart the key is back; io-threads is 1. SETBIT on 300,000 of 1,000,000 ids: BITCOUNT 300000, STRLEN 125000, MEMORY USAGE 163912 bytes.
claims.verified_by: Experiment run by the author on 2026-10-18 on one KVM virtual machine (4 vCPU): redis-cli against Redis 7.0.15 (Ubuntu package).

claims.claim_vi: Redis data structures suit counting clicks and comments (hash), sorting and deduplicating users (zset), behaviour history (zset, hash) and large boolean data in small space (bitmap).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung ghi chú: giống nhau, khác nhau đã thử, và ví dụ bitmap. Bảng so sánh đầy đủ nằm trong bài.
source_deviations: Source shows a comparison diagram and four Redis use cases; the lesson checks each difference by running both servers and measures the bitmap example. No speed comparison is made.
The restart row ran SAVE before restarting Redis; the lesson says so and notes that with default periodic snapshots a key just written may not survive a crash.
